about: The wreck as the game draws it beyond its made pieces: the planned ground out to the plan's edge and the ball under it, the base on the horizon (each module's own stage where the game stands it), the Earth in the sky, the sun and earthshine, the break light and the sky. Frame: the wreck's own seat.

turn.from: sky.gd:136-144,455-472 (_stars_turn: Space.frame_basis() transposed, the Moon's facing at the base minute), space.gd:76-80, orbits.gd:128-145,345-356 (Orbits.facing_at, _moon_own_frame), turned onto the place's seat (Seat.frame, tools/usd/ground.py); the Moon turns its stars round once a lap of 4,762.6 base minutes, under seven real minutes, so each game shot holds its own moment: measured by tools/usd/star_turn.py, the field identified on each and its turn matched to the facing, the minute (within the lap) taken from wreck-home (12 stars, 0.43 degrees off the facing); wreck-wake gives 649.5 (8 stars, 0.97), wreck-side 755.0 (7 stars, 0.40); the sun's minute is not measured, and the record's sun, set by eye to the shots' shadows, is off the true Sun's path at every minute

owner_rejected.what: the base's landing pad and its ring, and the old ship standing on its own pad with that pad's ring: the game draws them all
owner_rejected.why: the owner, playtesting on 2026-10-04, asked for the landing pad left beside the broken rocket and the old rocket still standing there to be deleted (the owner's playtest notes of 2026-10-04)

coordinator_removed.what: the supply rocket and cargo lift laid on the landing pad, and the landing dust thrown across it
coordinator_removed.why: the coordinator's call, not the owner's: they stood on the landing pad the owner rejected, and without it they would float over bare ground; the owner may bring them back
